title: Missing trend after the merge
description: Your trending pipeline spreads hashtag events round-robin over 20 shards. Each shard counts exactly and reports its top 100; an aggregator merges those 2,000 candidates into the final top 100. A tag with 400,000 uses this hour, split evenly across the shards, never appears. Why can this merge miss a major trend?

options.text: The aggregator should keep the top 200 instead of the top 100
options.explanation: A larger cut-off helps only by luck; with round-robin sharding a tag can rank low on every shard and still be missing, however many candidates each shard reports.

options.text: Switch each shard to a count-min sketch so counts are smaller
options.explanation: Sketches change memory use, not the merge logic; local top-K lists from non-key-partitioned shards are still the wrong inputs.

options.text: Increase the refresh interval so shards accumulate more data before reporting
options.explanation: More time does not change the fact that the tag's count is split twenty ways and is never in any local top 100.

options.text: Partition events by hash of the tag so each tag's full count lives on one shard, then merge local top-K lists; add per-tag pre-aggregation to protect against hot tags
options.explanation: With key partitioning, every global top-K tag must appear in its own shard's local top-K, so the union of local lists is guaranteed to contain the answer; combiners keep hot tags from overloading a shard.
